observations.first_contract: The public extremity entry validates the LimbArmorDesign, builds a recipe for mitten/sabaton/boot, and accepts a caller-supplied frame slice. Per-chart and per-coordinate shell lookup checks frame index with get().ok_or(InvalidSurface), so a reached missing index returns a typed error rather than indexing that frame slice unchecked. These checks do not validate frame-buffer size, alignment, finiteness, side, semantic fit or future native execution.
observations.conditional_partial_recording: A selected unfluted mitten places a cuff chart referencing frame0 in the recipe before its thumb chart referencing frame1; chart layout makes the cuff 13 rows × 40 columns = 520 items. PartRecipe records shells in insertion order. If a public caller provides only frame0, all earlier validation, construction, uploads and frame0 chart recording succeed, and the kernel uses a valid nonzero workgroup size, control reaches the later missing frame1 error after dispatch_items was called for the cuff. On the explicitly conditional fast-kernel branch, KernelBatch::dispatch records a compute pass into the caller-owned encoder before it increments dispatch count. The shown loop has no local rollback before returning the later error, and the caller still owns its mutable batch; the batch API exposes submit. A slow kernel separately calls ComputePass::record, whose body was not inspected here. No actual caller, invalid input, command, GPU, shader, batch submission or runtime behavior was executed. Whether a supported caller can supply one frame, whether it would reuse/submit after Err, and whether any resulting side effect matters are unresolved. The host build path shown owns a local batch and returns on record error before its explicit submit, but that does not prove all caller behavior.
observations.safeguards: The inspected DeviceWearer mitten path supplies both hand and thumb frame buffers; its sabaton/boot paths each supply one foot frame. The selected footwear toe/boot shells name frame0. Parent validation admits mitten finger lames 2–6 and sabaton lames 3–8, excluding a zero selected count when validation succeeds. This does not establish buffer contents or all APIs.
